newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue chips surrender gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue chips surrender gains at close.

text.p: Argentine blue chips gave back early gains and closed flat Tuesday as profit-taking followed closely on the heels of a successful global bond launch, dealers said.

"Prices first rose on the deal, but really the good news had already been discounted and players took advantage of the optimistic mood to take some profits," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers. "I think the market will resume its upward course tomorrow."
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index slipped off a high of 693.08 and closed unchanged at 686.61.
Technical analysts predicted it would stretch to between 700-710 in the short-term before facing a downward correction.
"The market will keep rising on the global bond momentum," another trader said.
Argentina announced Tuesday it placed $2.0 billion with a 20-year maturity at 462.5 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, and said the issue had been three times oversubscribed.
Traders said the bolsa would also be underpinned by Wall Street's positive reaction to upbeat statements by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan Tuesday on the state of the economy.
The broad market pared gains to 0.2 percent, with 40 risers, half as many decliners and 25 issues closing flat.

Floor volume recovered to 23.6 million pesos from a token tally of 9.6 million seen Monday during the U.S. Martin Luther King holiday. Over-the-counter deals also recovered to 100.1 million pesos from 20.5 million Monday.

Top main-tier performers were electricity stocks Central Puerto and Central Costanera, which jumped 3.6 percent and 2.8 percent each. Losers were led by textile firm Alpargatas, off 1.9 percent, and petrochemical firm Indupa, down 1.8 percent.
